chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ismāʿīl ibn Murrār, from Yūnus, from al-Khaṭṭāb ibn Salamah; and it was also narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Saʿīd, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, from al-Khaṭṭāb ibn Salamah, from Hishām ibn Aḥmad, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a mudabbar slave who killed a man by mistake. He said: “What have you narrated concerning this matter?”

He said: I said: We have narrated from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام that he said: “He is delivered with his rope to the heirs of the slain; then when the one who declared him mudabbar dies, he becomes free.”
He said: “Glory be to Allah! So the blood of a Muslim man would be nullified?” I said: This is how we have narrated it.
He said: “You have erred against my father. He is delivered with his rope to the heirs of the slain; then when the one who declared him mudabbar dies, he is made to work to pay his value.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal claimants of the slain person
key_terms.اسْتُسْعِيَ: he was required to work and earn
key_terms.دَمُ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ: the blood of a Muslim person, meaning his legally protected life
key_terms.مُدَبَّرٍ: a slave promised freedom upon the death of his master

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a mudabbar slave who kills a man by mistake in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling regarding a mudabbar slave who kills someone by mistake. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام corrects a mistaken transmission and clarifies that the offender is handed over to the heirs of the victim, and after the death of the one who declared him mudabbar, he must earn and pay his value rather than becoming immediately free. The report emphasizes the protection of Muslim blood and precision in transmitting legal hadith.
